lessons.title: Body Parts

items.example: Eu estou com dor de estômago.
Eu tenho um problema no olho.
items.exampleMeaning: I have a problem with my eye.

lessons.tip: In Brazilian Portuguese, nouns have genders. 'A' is used for feminine nouns and 'o' for masculine nouns. For example, 'a cabeça' (the head) is feminine, while 'o braço' (the arm) is masculine.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Eu estou com dor de cabeça.

scenario.partnerRole: a friend who is concerned about your health
scenario.learnerRole: someone who is not feeling well
scenario.brief: Your friend asks you about your health. Respond with what hurts and how you feel. Use the body parts you learned.
scenario.goal: You need to explain your symptoms.

lessons.title: What Hurts?
lessons.tip: When saying what hurts, use 'dói' with the body part. For example, 'A cabeça dói' means 'The head hurts.' This structure is common.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, eu tenho uma consulta médica.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have a doctor's appointment.

scenario.brief: You are at the doctor's office. The doctor asks you about your pain. Respond with where it hurts and if you have an appointment.
scenario.goal: You need to describe your pain to the doctor.

lessons.title: At the Pharmacy

items.exampleMeaning: I am going to buy medicine.

items.example: Eu vou tomar o remédio agora.
items.exampleMeaning: I will take the medicine now.

lessons.tip: When you want to express an action, use the verb in the infinitive form. For example, 'comprar' means 'to buy' and 'tomar' means 'to take.'

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Are you going to buy medicine?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I am going to buy medicine.

scenario.brief: You are at the pharmacy. Ask where it is and if they can help you with medicine. Use the vocabulary you learned.
scenario.goal: You need to ask for help at the pharmacy.

lessons.title: Giving Advice

items.exampleMeaning: It is important to drink water.
It is good to consult a doctor.

lessons.tip: To give advice, use 'deve' (should) followed by the verb. For example, 'Você deve descansar' means 'You should rest.'

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Is it important to take medicine?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, it is important to drink water.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, você deve ficar em casa.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, you should stay at home.

scenario.brief: Your friend asks for advice about their health. Use the vocabulary to give suggestions on what they should do.
scenario.goal: You need to give health advice.

review.title: Chapter Review: Health and the Doctor

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Eu estou com dor de estômago.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: You should go to the doctor.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, eu vou à farmácia comprar remédio.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I will go to the pharmacy to buy medicine.

scenario.brief: Your friend asks about your health and what you plan to do. Use the vocabulary from the chapter to explain your situation.
scenario.goal: You need to communicate your health issues and your next steps.
